children: Foreign investors bought long-term Japanese government bonds (JGBs) for a third straight week through September 5, drawn by rising domestic yields and prospects of a Bank of Japan interest rate hike.
They made a net purchase of 449.6 billion yen ($2.93 billion) in Japanese long-term bonds while selling a net 275.2 billion yen of short-term bills, data from Japan's Ministry of Finance showed.
The 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) rose to 3.015% last week, its highest since September 1996, fuelling speculation that Japanese investors may begin redirecting capital back home.
Hawkish comments from BOJ board member Hajime Takata and U.S. support for Japan taking "decisive" monetary action to address inflation and yen weakness boosted rate-hike expectations.

Foreign investors bought a net 690 million yen of Japanese stocks, the biggest weekly net purchase since July 25.
Japanese investors bought a net 111.9 billion yen of foreign long-term bonds after two straight weeks of selling. They purchased about 103.8 billion yen of short-term bills.
They sold 481.6 billion yen of overseas stocks after a modest purchase of 35.8 billion yen in the previous week.
